title: Side Quests Grow on Trees (Leave Them Where They Grow) 🌿
why_read: A nice-to-see hobby project combining on-device vision models for a children's plant-identification game, with a genuine privacy-conscious and safety-tested design.
analysis: This describes a native Android app that uses two small open-weight vision models, BioCLIP and TinyCLIP, running entirely on-device to help kids identify real plants during a treasure hunt game. It also uses a local Gemma 4 model offline during the build pipeline to generate hints, while final toxic-plant filtering relies on deterministic code rather than the AI model, which is a sensible safety design choice given the stated zero false-positive result on 267 toxic plant test photos. It's a fairly small-scope hobby/hackathon submission, but the on-device multi-model pipeline and safety-conscious architecture are genuinely interesting for mobile ML practitioners.
